newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee tracks weaker NY to finish lower.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee tracks weaker NY to finish lower.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures reversed an earlier upward trend to finish Thursday with pared losses after New York arabicas took a tumble on chart-driven speculative selling.

Traders said forecasts for mild temperatures in Brazil's coffee belt and news of 10,3985 bags pending grading in New York triggered the sell-off in arabica futures. At 1608 GMT, New York September was 11.15 cents down at 169.00 cents a lb.
But losses in robustas were less severe, partly due to the prolonged absence of origin selling pressure.
"Origins are unlikely to follow the market down. Anyway producers such as Indonesia don't have a big crop," said one trader.
But trade is still generally short and roasters still have some buying to do, albeit at much lower levels.
By the close, September stood $49 down at $1,801 a tonne after ranging between $1,780 and $1,889.
July, the other active month, gave up $37 at $1,795. July/Sept spread which was quoted at $17-$20 earlier, stood at a narrow $6 at the close.
Traders said the market seemed to have lost a clear direction after the recent sharp downward correction from the highs seen in late May.
"It has to find a base somewhere instead of wandering around," said one trader. He saw the market building a base at between $1,715 and $1,800 basis September and trade up from there.
Trading enthusiasm this month has also been dampened by concern over the new LIFFE coffee quality-grading scheme.

LIFFE told members on Wednesday it would review the grading criteria for coffee following complaints from the trade that the terms had resulted in large amounts of coffee being graded as non-tenderable.
But pending the outcome of the review, the controversial ruling on the specific defect count for mouldy beans would continue to be enforced.
So far this month, some 72 percent of beans put up for grading had failed the rigorous test.
Overall volume reached 4,991 lots. Options were fairly active with 2,002 lots changing hands, centred on September $1,700, $1,800, $1,900 and $2,000 calls.
